_comment: Config for scripts/mr_conflict_watch.py. No credentials here -- glab holds its own GitLab auth (glab auth login), same as every other skill that shells out to it.
_skip_draft_mrs_note: Draft MRs are usually mid-build in another chain's worktree -- resolving conflicts on a moving target wastes a run. Re-evaluated every poll tick, so it picks up automatically once marked ready.
_skip_labels_note: MRs carrying any of these labels are left alone entirely, regardless of conflict state. 'needs-human' is applied BY the resolver skill itself on escalation -- a human removes it (after resolving or accepting the conflict by hand) to make the MR eligible again. 'wip' is a manual founder marker for 'don't touch this one'.
_resolver_model_note: Conflict assessment plus real git/test work -- Sonnet, same tier as the build stage in .agents/model-routing.json. Not Haiku: this skill edits code when a conflict is genuinely semantic, which triage-only skills (slack-watcher) never do.
_resolver_permission_mode_note: The resolver needs real Bash (git, pytest, ruff, glab) and Edit, but every MR it acts on originated from an unattended run -- so 'auto' (classifier-gated) rather than 'acceptEdits' (unrestricted), matching slack_watch.py's chain_permission_mode. It never merges or force-pushes; those stay barred regardless of this setting.
_agent_timeout_note: 30 minutes. Covers worktree setup, a merge, a scoped test/lint pass, and a push -- generous because a real semantic conflict may need re-reading both sides' intent before touching anything.
_crash_grace_note: Added to agent_timeout_sec before a 'handed_off' MR is treated as a dead run and retried. Covers the gap between the process actually finishing and the watchdog updating state.
_max_attempts_note: Per MR, per head sha. A conflict that can't be resolved in 3 attempts on the same commit is not going to resolve on a 4th -- mark stalled and let a human look, same reasoning as slack_watch's per-thread retry cap. A new push resets the counter (new sha, new question).
_quota_preflight_ceiling_pct_note: Shared with slack_watch.py's quota gate (scripts/mr_conflict_watch.py imports it directly) -- don't launch a resolver run if the cached 5h reading is already at/above this.
_quota_cache_max_age_sec_note: A cached reading older than this is treated as absent, never as a reason to hold -- same reasoning as slack-watch.json.
_quota_fallback_window_sec_note: 5 hours. Estimate used when there is no fresh cached reading -- e.g. the watchdog detecting a mid-run quota failure with no recent interactive render to confirm against.
